# Free GST Billing Software: complete documentation (version 1.10.81)

Source: /docs/

---

# Free GST Billing documentation

URL: /docs/

Make GST invoices, keep track of who owes you, and prepare your GST returns. On your own computer, with no account and no monthly fee.

- [Install it Download, extract, click Install. About three minutes, no admin rights needed.](/docs/install.html)
- [Make your first invoice From a blank app to a GST tax invoice you can send, in five minutes.](/docs/first-invoice.html)
- [Something isn't working The common problems, what causes each one, and the fix.](/docs/troubleshooting.html)

## What it does

Free GST Billing is invoicing and GST software for small businesses in India, and for anyone billing in other currencies: 20 are supported. It runs on your computer and opens in your web browser, the way a website does, but nothing leaves your machine.

- **Invoices**: tax invoices, bills of supply, proforma estimates, credit notes and delivery challans, with CGST, SGST, IGST and UTGST worked out for you.
- **Getting paid**: record payments, print receipts, see who is overdue and by how much.
- **GST returns**: GSTR-1 and GSTR-3B built from your invoices and purchases, as files you upload to the GST portal.
- **The rest of the books**: clients, products and stock, purchases, expenses, recurring invoices, profit and loss, and an income tax calculator.

## What you need

| Computer | Windows 10 or 11, macOS, or Linux (a NAS works too). |

| Browser | Chrome, Edge, Firefox or Brave. The app opens in it. |

| Disk space | Roughly 200 MB once installed. |

| Internet | Only for the first install and for updates. Everything else works offline. |

| Account or signup | None. |

## Where your data lives

Every invoice, client and setting is saved as plain files inside the app's folder, in _system\data. They never leave your computer unless you turn on Google Drive backup yourself.

That also means backing up is your job, and it is easy. See [Backups, updates and moving PC](/docs/backup.html).

## Is it really free?

Yes. It is open source under the MIT licence. There is no trial, no invoice limit, no feature that unlocks for money, and no advertising. The code is public on [GitHub](https://github.com/OmRaj6666/GST-Billing-Software-LIFE-TIME-USE-NO-Subscription-Required-), so anyone can check what it does.

## Getting help

Every screen in the app with a ? button links to the matching part of these pages. If something is missing here, or the app does something these pages don't describe, [open an issue on GitHub](https://github.com/OmRaj6666/GST-Billing-Software-LIFE-TIME-USE-NO-Subscription-Required-/issues) with a screenshot. Many features began as someone's request.

# Install

URL: /docs/install.html

Download one ZIP, extract it, open the launcher for your computer and click Install. On Windows it sets up everything it needs by itself.

## Download

Download the ZIP. The link always gives you the newest version.

[Download Free GST Billing](https://github.com/OmRaj6666/GST-Billing-Software-LIFE-TIME-USE-NO-Subscription-Required-/releases/latest/download/Free-GST-Billing.zip)

**Use this link, not GitHub's green Code button**
The green Code button on GitHub gives you the source code, not the app. It will not install.

## Install on Windows

- **Extract the ZIP**Right-click the downloaded file and choose Extract All…, then Extract. Put it somewhere you will remember, such as Documents.
- **Open the launcher**In the new folder, double-click **Free GST Billing - WINDOWS**. Each launcher is named after the computer it is for.
- **Click Install**A small window opens with one button. Click Install. There is nothing to fill in.
- **Wait for the browser**A black window does the work and closes by itself. It takes one to three minutes the first time. The app then opens in your browser at http://localhost:47371.

Before install, the launcher shows one button. Afterwards it shows Open App, and everything else is under More options.

## Extract the ZIP before opening anything

Windows lets you double-click a file while you are still looking inside a ZIP. When you do, it copies just that one file to a temporary folder and runs it there, so the rest of the app is not next to it.

The launcher notices this and says Please extract the ZIP first, with a button that opens your Downloads folder. Close it, extract the ZIP, and open the launcher from the extracted folder.

## "Windows protected your PC"

You may see this blue warning the first time. It appears for software that is not signed with a paid certificate, which costs a few hundred dollars a year and would make a free app not free.

- Click More info.
- Click Run anyway.

If the file will not open at all, right-click **Free GST Billing - WINDOWS**, choose Properties, tick Unblock at the bottom, and click OK.

If your antivirus removes a file during install, add the app's folder to its exclusions and click Install again.

## What the installer does

- **Sets up Node.js inside the app folder**, if your PC does not already have it. Node.js is the engine the app runs on. It is downloaded once (about 30 MB) from nodejs.org and kept in _system\node. Nothing is installed into Windows, and no administrator rights are needed.
- **Downloads the app's building blocks** from the internet. This is the only other download.
- **Puts a Free GST Billing shortcut** on your Desktop and in the Start menu, with the app's icon.
- **Opens the app** in your browser when it is done.

If you already have Node.js, the installer uses yours and leaves it alone.

## Install with one command (optional)

If you are comfortable with a terminal, this does all of the above. Open PowerShell and paste:

```
irm https://raw.githubusercontent.com/OmRaj6666/GST-Billing-Software-LIFE-TIME-USE-NO-Subscription-Required-/main/install.ps1 | iex
```

It installs to %LOCALAPPDATA%\Programs\Free GST Billing. To choose another folder, run this first:

```
$env:FREEGSTBILL_DIR = 'D:\Apps\Free GST Billing'
```

If the app is already installed in that folder with data in it, the command stops and tells you to update from inside the app instead, so it can never write over your books.

## Install on a Mac

On a Mac, Node.js has to be installed first. It is free.

- **Install Node.js**Download the installer from [nodejs.org](https://nodejs.org/en/download), or if you use Homebrew, run brew install node@20.
- **Extract the ZIP**Double-click the downloaded ZIP. macOS extracts it next to the download.
- **Open the launcher**In the folder, open **Free GST Billing - MAC**. If macOS says it is from an unidentified developer, right-click it, choose Open, then Open again.
- **Let it finish**A Terminal window sets the app up the first time, then opens it in your browser.

## Install on Linux or a NAS

As on a Mac, install Node.js 18 or newer first, for example sudo apt install nodejs npm. Then:

```
unzip Free-GST-Billing.zip
cd Free-GST-Billing
chmod +x "Free GST Billing - LINUX.sh"
./"Free GST Billing - LINUX.sh"
```

The app then runs at http://localhost:47371. To update later from inside the app, the system also needs unzip or python3.

## The first time the app opens

A short welcome asks for your business details and bank or UPI, then offers to set up your invoices for your kind of business. See [The first-run setup](/docs/first-run.html).

## Opening the app every day

Double-click the **Free GST Billing** shortcut on your Desktop, then Open App. The launcher is also where you update, back up, restore, and move to another PC, under More options.

**Keep the launcher**
It is the one file you need. You never have to download anything again to update; the launcher does it for you.

## Removing the app

Nothing is installed into Windows itself, so removing the app is just deleting it:

- **Back up your data first** if you might want it again. See [Export everything to one file](/docs/backup.html#export-import).
- In the launcher, open More options and click Stop the app.
- Delete the app's folder, and the **Free GST Billing** shortcuts on the Desktop and in the Start menu.

# The first-run setup

URL: /docs/first-run.html

The screens you see the first time the app opens: a four-step welcome for your business details, then a three-step setup for how your invoices look. Both can be skipped and changed later.

## Step 1 of the welcome: where you invoice from

The first screen explains what the app does, and asks **Where will you be invoicing from?**

| 🇮🇳 India | GST, GSTR-1 and 3B, UPI. The default. |

| 🌍 Outside India | VAT and other local taxes |

| 🌐 Both | India, with clients abroad |

Get Started carries on. Skip Setup goes straight to the app; fill in [Settings](/docs/settings.html#company-details) later.

## Step 2: business details

These print at the top of every invoice. Only the **Business Name** is required.

| Business Name | Required |

| Address | Your full address |

| State | Needed to work out CGST and SGST versus IGST |

| GSTIN | Leave blank if you are not registered |

| PAN, Phone, Email | Optional |

## Step 3: bank and UPI

Where clients should pay you: bank name, account number, IFSC code and UPI ID. A UPI ID puts a scan-to-pay QR code on your invoices. You can also upload your logo and signature here, up to 500 KB each. Skip, I’ll add later leaves it all for [Settings](/docs/settings.html#payment-accounts).

## Step 4: you're all set

A short list of what to do next. Start Billing saves everything; your bank details become your first [payment account](/docs/settings.html#payment-accounts).

## Then: setting up your invoices

Next, a three-step window sets up printing.

- **What kind of business do you run?**Pick one of six: Retail Shop / Kirana, Freelancer / Consultant, Restaurant / Cafe / Bar, Wholesale / Trading, Manufacturing, or Service / Repair Shop. Each sets the invoice style, receipt options and features that suit that business. See [Business type](/docs/print-settings.html#business-type) for exactly what each one sets. Or choose **None of these** to set things up yourself.
- **Paper size and language**Pick what you mostly print on: A4, A5, 80 mm or 58 mm thermal. It becomes the paper size of new invoices. Then the language for section labels such as BILL TO: English, Hindi, Tamil, Marathi or Bengali.
- **Ready to go**A summary of your choices. Finish setup applies them.

Skip setup, or the ✕, closes it. A ✨ Finish setup button then waits at the bottom right of the screen, for whenever you want to come back to it. Everything it sets can also be changed in [Print and PDF settings](/docs/print-settings.html).

---

# Your first invoice

URL: /docs/first-invoice.html

From a blank app to a GST tax invoice you can send, in about five minutes.

## Before you start

Have these to hand: your business name, address and GSTIN, and your bank account or UPI ID if you want clients to pay you directly from the invoice. None of it is compulsory, and all of it can be added later.

## Make the invoice

- **Add your business details**If you skipped the welcome, open Settings and fill in **Company Details**. This is the header of every invoice. Your state matters: it decides whether GST is split into CGST and SGST, or charged as IGST.
- **Start a new invoice**Click New Invoice in the sidebar. **Tax Invoice** is already selected, which is the right choice for a normal GST sale.
- **Add the client**Under **Billed To**, type the client's name. If they are registered for GST, type their GSTIN and their state fills in by itself. A mistyped GSTIN is caught straight away.
- **Add what you sold**For each line, give a description, quantity, unit, rate and GST rate. The HSN or SAC code is optional but helps your GST return. Clicking a number field selects what is there, so you can just type.
- **Check the tax**The preview on the right shows the totals. Same state as you: CGST and SGST. Another state: IGST. You do not need to choose.
- **Save and download**Click Save & Download. The invoice gets its number, is saved to your records, and downloads as a PDF.

## Send it

- WhatsApp opens a message to the client. On a phone the PDF is attached for you; on a computer, WhatsApp does not let websites attach files, so download the PDF and drag it into the chat.
- Print opens your printer directly, including thermal receipt printers.
- Or attach the downloaded PDF to an email yourself.

## When the client pays

On the [Dashboard](/docs/dashboard.html), find the invoice and record the payment. A printable receipt opens straight away, and the invoice's status changes to **Partial** or **Paid**. Unpaid invoices past their due date are marked **Overdue** for you.

## What to do next

- [Add your products and services](/docs/products.html), so you pick them from a list instead of typing them each time.
- [Add your bank or UPI](/docs/settings.html#payment-accounts), so a payment QR code prints on every invoice.
- [Add your logo, signature and stamp](/docs/settings.html#branding).
- At the end of the month, [prepare your GST returns](/docs/gst-returns.html) from the invoices you have made.

The **Getting started** list on the Dashboard tracks these for you, and ticks each one off once it is done.

---

# Making an invoice

URL: /docs/invoices.html

Every part of the New Invoice screen, from top to bottom: the toolbar, the document type, the client, the items, terms, extra pages, and what happens when you save, print or share.

## How the screen is laid out

Open it with New Invoice in the sidebar, or Ctrl + N. The form is on the left and a live preview of the printed invoice is on the right. From top to bottom, the form has these cards:

- **Invoice Type**, with the Customize panel when it is open
- **Billed To**: the client
- **Invoice Details**: number, dates, place of supply and delivery address
- **Line Items**
- **Terms & Conditions**, notes and a private note
- **Additional Pages / Sections**

The totals are not in the form. They are worked out as you type and shown in the preview.

## The toolbar

The toolbar stays at the top of the screen as you scroll.

| Button | What it does |

| ← Back | Leaves the invoice. If you have changed something that is not saved, you are asked first (see Leaving with unsaved changes ). |

| ? | A short how-to for this screen. |

| Save status | Shows **Draft - click to complete** until the invoice has a client and an item (click it to jump to what is missing), then **Not saved yet** until you first save it, then **Saving…**, **All changes saved** or **Ready**. |

| Save | Saves the invoice without making a PDF. Ctrl + S does the same. |

| Save & Download | Saves the invoice and downloads the PDF. See Save & Download . |

| Print | Saves the invoice, then prints it. See Printing . |

| WhatsApp | Opens WhatsApp with the invoice details typed in. See Sending on WhatsApp . |

| E-Way Bill | Tax invoices and delivery challans only. Downloads the e-way bill file. See E-way bill . |

| Customize | Opens the panel that controls what prints, the paper size, currency and more. See [Customize: what prints and how](/docs/invoice-options.html). |

| Hide Preview | Hides the preview so the form uses the whole width, handy for long invoices. Show Preview brings it back, and the app remembers your choice. |

## Choosing the document type

The six chips at the top decide the printed title, whether GST is charged, and whether the document counts as a sale in your totals and returns.

| Type | Prints as | Use it for | GST | Counts as a sale? |

| Tax Invoice | TAX INVOICE | A normal sale by a GST-registered business | Yes | Yes |

| Quotation | QUOTATION | A priced offer for work or supply, numbered QUO/…. Convert it to a tax invoice when the client accepts. | Shown | No |

| Proforma / Estimate | PROFORMA INVOICE | A quote before the sale. Prints "This is not a tax invoice" and a faint ESTIMATE watermark. | Shown | No |

| Bill of Supply (No GST) | BILL OF SUPPLY | Exempt goods or services | No | Yes |

| Composition (Bill of Supply) | BILL OF SUPPLY | Sales under the composition scheme. The declaration required by Rule 46A prints automatically. | No | Yes |

| Credit Note | CREDIT NOTE | Returns, a price cut after the sale, or a correction. Its total is subtracted from your sales. | Yes | Subtracted |

| Delivery Challan | DELIVERY CHALLAN | Moving goods without a sale, such as to a job worker or on approval | No | No |

There are seven types. Changing the type also changes the invoice number to that type's series, replacing any number you typed.

**Once an invoice is saved, its type is locked.** The other chips are greyed out, because the number and the tax already issued to your client must not change. To make a different document from it, use Duplicate on the Dashboard.

## Goods, services or both

Under the type chips, **This invoice is for** sets which units you are offered:

| 📦 Goods | Units such as Nos, Kg and Pcs. The default. |

| ⏱ Services | Hours, sessions, visits and months. It also reminds you to put a SAC code in the HSN field. |

| 🔀 Mixed | Every unit, unfiltered. |

## Billed To: the client

- **Type the name**Clicking **Client Name** lists your saved clients. As you type, the list narrows. Use ↓ ↑ and Enter, or click one. Picking a saved client fills in all their details.
- **Or save a new one**For someone new, type their name and fill in the fields, then click **Save "name" as new client** to keep them for next time. You do not have to: an invoice can go to a name that is not saved.
- **Check the address and GSTIN**Address, country, city, PIN, state and GSTIN print on the invoice.

A saved client's pencil icon opens their details for editing. Their email, phone and **SEZ** setting are only edited there, not on the invoice: see [Adding and editing a client](/docs/clients.html#client-form). A client can also have a preferred paper size, currency and auto-print setting, which are applied when you pick them on a new invoice.

Changing the **country** clears the state, since each country has its own list.

## What the GSTIN check tells you

When you leave the GSTIN box, the app reads the number. This works offline, with no GST portal lookup.

| Message | Meaning |

| ✓ Registered in state . State filled in. | The state was blank, so it has been filled in from the first two digits. |

| ✓ Registered in state . | The GSTIN and the state agree. |

| ⚠ This GSTIN is registered in state , but the state says other state . | Check which is right. The tax split follows the state and place of supply. |

| ⚠ This GSTIN fails its own checksum. Check for a typo. | Every GSTIN ends with a check character. This one does not add up, so a character is almost certainly mistyped. |

These are warnings only. They never stop you saving.

## Using a client's credit

If the client overpaid on earlier invoices, a banner shows how much credit they have and where it came from. On a new invoice you can:

- type an amount to use, or click Apply full to use as much as this invoice needs;
- click Skip to use none;
- tick **Auto-apply available client credit on future invoices** to have it used automatically.

When you save, the credit is recorded as a payment on this invoice.

## Invoice Details

| Field | What to know |

| Invoice Number | Filled in with the next number for this type. It is only taken when you first save, so an invoice you abandon does not use up a number. If someone else's invoice took it meanwhile, yours gets the next free number and you are told. See [Invoice number format](/docs/settings.html#invoice-numbers). |

| Invoice Date | Today, unless you change it. |

| Due Date | Blank unless you set it. Once it passes, an unpaid invoice becomes **Overdue**. |

| Place of Supply | Where the goods or services are supplied. Leave it on **Defaults to Client State** unless the delivery is in a different state from the client's address. The tax split follows it. Not shown for bills of supply, composition bills or delivery challans. |

| Original Invoice Reference | Credit notes only: the invoice it is against, such as INV/2026-27/0001. It prints as "Against Invoice". |

| Ship to same as bill-to address | Ticked by default. Untick it to enter a delivery address, city, PIN and state. The invoice then prints a separate **SHIP TO** block. |

## Order, dispatch and reference details

Under Invoice Details, **Order, dispatch & reference details** opens a set of optional fields, the boxes a Tally invoice carries:

work details, revision no, vehicle no, service period from and to, buyer's order no and order date, reference no & date, other references, delivery note and its date, dispatch doc no, dispatched through, destination, mode or terms of payment, and terms of delivery.

Only what you fill in prints. The [Tally style](/docs/invoice-options.html#style) design shows them in its reference boxes; the other designs list them under Bill To. The section stays open on an invoice that has any of them.

## Line items

Each row has these fields:

| Field | What to know |

| Description | The item name. Typing searches your [products](/docs/products.html) by name or HSN; picking one fills in the HSN, rate, unit and GST rate, and links the row to the product so its stock is counted. |

| HSN/SAC | For common codes the app knows the usual GST rate, and shows it in green under the box. If the row's rate is still 18% or 0%, it is changed to match. |

| Qty | 1 to start. Clicking the box selects the number, so typing replaces it. |

| Unit | From the list for Goods, Services or Mixed. ＋ Add custom… adds your own unit (up to 20 characters), marked ★, and − Remove takes it away again. Invoices already made keep the unit they used. |

| Rate | Price for one unit. |

| Discount | An amount (₹) or a percentage (%) of the line. For an amount, a second box chooses what it comes off: **Net**, the line total (the default); **Unit**, that much off each unit; or **W/Tax**, off the total including tax. |

| GST % | 0, 0.1, 0.25, 3, 5, 12, 18, 28 or 40%, plus any rates you added in [Print Settings](/docs/print-settings.html#tax-rates). Custom… takes any rate from 0 to 100. New rows start at 18%. Since 22 September 2025 most goods are at 5%, 18% or 40%; 12% and 28% stay for older invoices and the items still taxed at them. |

| Cess % | Compensation cess, for tobacco, cars, coal and the like. Hidden until you turn on **GST Cess % column** under Customize. |

- + Add description under a row adds a longer note that prints under the item name.
- Add Item adds a row. So does pressing Enter in the last row once it has something in it.
- Delivery charges adds the charge as its own line, SAC 996812, taxed at the highest GST rate among the goods on the invoice (delivery that comes with goods is taxed like them). Type the amount in its Rate. It is in the total and GST returns and never touches stock. Change its GST % if your delivery is a separate service.
- The bin removes a row. The last remaining row cannot be removed.
- Hiding a column under Customize, such as HSN or Discount, also hides it here.

## Prices that already include GST

If your rates already include GST, tick **Prices include tax** at the top of the Line Items card. The printed Subtotal is then the value before tax, so Subtotal + tax = Total. The GST is then worked out backwards from each rate, and the invoice shows the taxable value and the tax separately.

## Discounts

- **On a line**: in the row's Discount box, as described above. This is the GST-correct way, because the discount comes off before tax.
- **On the whole bill**: **Discount on total**, under the items, as an amount or a percentage. It is taken off after tax, so it does not reduce the GST.

## How GST is worked out

You never choose between CGST, SGST and IGST. The app decides from your state and the place of supply:

| Situation | Charged as |

| Client in your state | CGST + SGST, half each |

| Client in another state | IGST |

| Within a Union Territory without a legislature (Chandigarh, Ladakh, Lakshadweep, Andaman and Nicobar, Dadra and Nagar Haveli and Daman and Diu) | CGST + UTGST |

| SEZ client, or a client outside India | IGST |

The preview shows **Intrastate (CGST + SGST)** or **Interstate (IGST)** next to the place of supply, so you can check it before saving.

**Your own state must be set**
If your business state is blank in [Settings](/docs/settings.html#company-details), the app warns you once and does not guess, because a wrong guess would charge the wrong tax on every invoice.

## Reverse charge

When the buyer pays the GST instead of you, under section 9(3) or 9(4), open Customize and tick **Reverse Charge applies** under Compliance flags. The invoice then says Reverse Charge: Yes and prints a notice that the recipient pays the GST. Every tax invoice and credit note prints Reverse Charge Yes or No, as the rules require.

## TDS and TCS

Both are under Customize, for Indian businesses. Turn on **TDS / TCS on invoices** in [Settings, Modules](/docs/settings.html#modules) first; it is off to begin with.

- **TCS**, tax you collect: tick it and pick the section: CGST section 52 (1%, e-commerce operators), 206C(1), or a custom rate. TCS is added to the invoice total. Section 206C(1H), TCS on sale of goods, was removed from 1 April 2025, so new invoices cannot choose it; invoices already made with it keep it.
- **TDS**, tax your client deducts: tick it and pick the section, such as 194Q, 194C, 194J, 194I, 194H, 194O or 195. It is for information: the invoice shows **Less: TDS** and the **Net Receivable**, and the total does not change.

Both are worked out on the amount including GST.

- **194Q** (and 206C(1H) on invoices before April 2025) only applies above ₹50 lakh a year with that client. The app adds up what you have already billed the client this financial year, and charges only the part above ₹50 lakh.
- **Every other section**, such as 194C, 194J or CGST section 52, applies from the first rupee. Tick it only when the rules say it applies to this client.

Invoices with TDS or TCS are summed in [the TDS / TCS report](/docs/gst-returns.html#tds-tcs). Have your CA confirm which sections apply to you.

## Billing in another currency

Under Customize, **Currency** offers 20 currencies, each with its own symbol and amount in words. For anything other than rupees you can enter the **exchange rate** for the day. It is kept with the invoice, so later reports stay right even when rates change, and it prints as an EXCHANGE RATE line.

The UPI QR code only prints on rupee invoices.

## Terms, notes and a private note

- **Terms & Conditions**: a text box with **B**, I, U, bulleted and numbered lists, headings, links and ✕ to clear formatting.
- **Insert preset** fills in starter wording for your kind of business: generic trader, freelancer, manufacturer or wholesaler, retail shop, restaurant, IT services, construction, medical, education and coaching, transport, real estate and rental, e-commerce seller, or export under LUT. If you already have terms, you are asked once before they are replaced.
- **Load saved template** uses one of [your saved templates](/docs/settings.html#terms). On a new invoice, your first template is loaded automatically.
- **PDF layout**: **Compact** prints the terms and notes small, to save paper; **Formatted** prints them as readable paragraphs.
- **Notes / Remarks** print on the invoice, for the client.
- **Private Note** is only for you, such as "follow up on the 20th". It never prints. On the Dashboard, a yellow note icon next to the client shows it.

## Extra pages

Under **Additional Pages / Sections**, + Add Section adds a titled section, such as a scope of work or delivery timeline. Each one prints as its own page after the invoice. You can paste formatted text, lists and tables from Word or Google Docs, and use the arrows to change the order.

## The live preview

The preview shows the invoice exactly as it will print, with the paper size, style and options you chose. − and + zoom out and in from 50% to 200%, and Fit fits it to the space. A saved invoice that has been cancelled shows CANCELLED across it.

## What must be filled in

A new invoice needs a **client name** and **at least one item** with a description, quantity and rate. Otherwise Save, Save & Download and Print tell you what is missing.

## Save & Download

Save & Download does all of this in one go:

- Saves the invoice, giving a new invoice its number, and counts it as printed once more.
- Downloads the PDF, showing that saved number, named after the type and number, such as INV_INV-2026-27-0001.pdf.
- Keeps a copy of the PDF in the app's Saved Invoices folder, in a folder for that client.
- Uploads it to Google Drive, if you have connected Drive in [Settings](/docs/settings.html#google-drive).
- Prints it, if auto-print is on in [Print Settings](/docs/print-settings.html#auto-print) or for this client.

Saving takes the items out of stock, for rows picked from your products; saving again after changing a quantity moves only the difference, and a quotation or proforma moves none (see [How stock is counted](/docs/products.html#stock)). If stock runs low or out, you are told.

If you change an invoice you have already downloaded or printed, a plain Save also updates its PDF in the Saved Invoices folder, without downloading it again.

Long invoices are split between rows, never through a row, and the signature and stamp are never cut across a page break: if they would be, the whole footer moves to the next page.

## Printing

- **On A4, A5 and other sheet sizes**, Print opens your browser's print window.
- **On a thermal paper size**, it first shows a **Print preview** of the receipt, with Print, Download PDF and Cancel. See [Thermal receipt printing](/docs/thermal-printing.html).

Printing saves the invoice first, like Save & Download, so what you hand the client is always in your records with the same number.

## Sending on WhatsApp

WhatsApp opens WhatsApp with the invoice number, date, client, subtotal and total typed in, and your business name. If the client is saved with a phone number, the chat opens with them; otherwise you choose the contact.

From the invoice screen the PDF is not attached. Download it with Save & Download and drag it into the chat. The WhatsApp button on the [Dashboard](/docs/dashboard.html#row-actions) can attach the PDF on phones.

## E-way bill

For tax invoices and delivery challans, E-Way Bill downloads a file, such as EWB-INV-2026-27-0001.json, in the format the NIC e-way bill portal accepts. Upload it there instead of typing everything again. Your own GSTIN must be set in Settings first. An e-way bill is generally needed when goods worth more than ₹50,000 are moved.

## Saving as you go

- What you type is kept while the browser tab stays open. If you leave the screen by mistake and come back, the invoice is still there.
- A **new** invoice is not stored in your records until you first click Save, Save & Download or Print. Until then the badge says **Not saved yet**.
- After that, changes are saved automatically about two seconds after you stop typing.

## Leaving with unsaved changes

If you click Back with unsaved changes, you choose Keep editing, Discard & leave or Save & leave. Closing or reloading the browser tab asks too.

## Keyboard shortcuts on this screen

| Ctrl + S | Save |

| Ctrl + P | Save and download the PDF (not print) |

| Ctrl + Enter | Add an item row |

| Ctrl + Shift + D | Duplicate the last row |

| Enter in the last row | Add a row |

| ↑ ↓ Enter | Pick from the client or product suggestions |

| Esc | Close suggestions or a dialog |

On a Mac, use ⌘ instead of Ctrl. More shortcuts: [Shortcuts, search and notifications](/docs/shortcuts.html).

## How to make a credit note

- **Start a new invoice**Choose **Credit Note** as the type.
- **Point it at the original**In **Original Invoice Reference**, enter the number of the invoice it corrects.
- **Enter what is being credited**Add the returned items, or the price difference, with the same GST rates as the original.
- **Save**Its total is subtracted from your sales on the Dashboard, and it goes into GSTR-1 as a credit note.

## Turning a quote into an invoice

When a client accepts a Quotation or a Proforma / Estimate, click Convert to Tax Invoice on it in the Dashboard. A new tax invoice opens with the same client and items, and gets its own number when you save it. The same works for a delivery challan. Once saved, the original shows **Converted** and its Convert button goes away, so it cannot be turned into a second invoice by mistake.

## Cancelling an invoice

An invoice number, once issued, has to stay in your records, so a saved invoice is cancelled rather than deleted. Cancel it from the [Dashboard](/docs/dashboard.html#cancel): it keeps its number, prints with CANCELLED across it, drops out of your totals and GST returns, and its stock goes back.

To correct an invoice already sent to a client, the GST way is a credit note rather than a cancellation.

---

# Customize: what prints and how

URL: /docs/invoice-options.html

The Customize panel on the invoice screen: title, currency, style, colour, every show-or-hide option, paper size and thermal settings, and exactly what each part of the printed invoice shows.

## Your choices become the default

Open the panel with Customize in the invoice toolbar. Whatever you change here is used for this invoice **and remembered for your next new invoice**, including the title, reverse charge, TDS and TCS. If a setting was only meant for one invoice, change it back afterwards.

A saved invoice keeps the options it was saved with.

These are per-invoice settings. The app-wide look, such as fonts, watermarks, copies and translated labels, is in [Print and PDF settings](/docs/print-settings.html).

## Title, currency and exchange rate

| Invoice Title | Replaces the printed title, such as TAX INVOICE. Leave it blank to use the type's own title. Thermal receipts ignore it. |

| Currency | Rupees to start. See [Billing in another currency](/docs/invoices.html#currency). |

| Exchange Rate | Only for currencies other than rupees. Kept with the invoice. |

## Make this a recurring invoice

Tick **🔁 Make this a recurring invoice** to have the app create this invoice again on a schedule, with the same client, items and amounts, a new number and that day's date.

| Frequency | Weekly, Monthly (the default), Quarterly or Yearly |

| Every N | 1 to 12. Monthly with 3 means every three months. |

| Next invoice date | One month after this invoice, to start |

| End condition | **Never (until I stop it)**, **On a specific date**, or **After N invoices**, for example 12 for a one-year monthly contract |

The schedule is saved when you save the invoice, and can be paused or changed from [Recurring](/docs/recurring.html).

## TCS, TDS and the payment account

- **TCS** and **TDS**: see [TDS and TCS](/docs/invoices.html#tds-tcs).
- **Payment account on this invoice**: if you have more than one bank account, choose which one prints. New invoices start with your ⭐ default account. The bank details and UPI QR are copied onto the invoice when you save it, so changing the account in Settings later never changes an invoice you have already sent.

## PDF style and accent colour

| Style | Look |

| Classic | Clean, with a coloured bar across the top. The default. |

| Modern | A solid colour block behind your business name, with the logo in white. |

| Minimal | Simple, with no borders. |

| Boxed grid | Every section in ruled boxes: your name large at the top, seller and document details side by side, Billing To and Shipping To, a Work Details line, and an item table filled with empty rows to a fixed height, like a printed quotation pad. |

| Tally style | The Tally layout: reference and dispatch boxes beside your details, state names with their codes, taxes inside the item table, amount in words with E. & O.E, an HSN/SAC tax summary, tax amount in words, your PAN, a declaration, and a "Customer's Seal and Signature" box. |

Tally style (left) and Boxed grid (right), with a made-up business.

**Accent Color**: **Auto** gives each type its own colour, such as blue for tax invoices, purple for proformas, teal for bills of supply and red for credit notes. You can also choose one of eight fixed colours: blue, purple, teal, red, orange, green, sky or dark.

## Showing and hiding parts of the invoice

Each tick box shows or hides one part of the printed invoice. Hiding something never deletes it.

| Group | Options | Off to start |

| Header & branding | Logo, business name, address, phone, email, state, Tax ID (GSTIN) | |

| Client / Bill-to | Client address, phone, email, Place of Supply | |

| Invoice meta | Invoice number, invoice date, due date | |

| Items table | HSN/SAC column, Qty column, unit next to the quantity, Rate column, Discount column, Tax % column, GST Cess % column | GST Cess |

| Totals | Subtotal row, amount in words, round-off line, HSN/SAC tax summary table, tax amount in words | The HSN summary and tax in words are on only in Tally style. Round-off follows [Print & PDF](/docs/print-settings.html#round-off) (on for new installs). |

| Compliance flags | Reverse Charge applies | Reverse Charge |

| Footer | Bank details, "Pay via" account label, UPI QR, signature block, "Authorized Signatory" caption, Terms & Conditions, Notes, system-generated note, Declaration, "Customer's Seal and Signature" box | "Pay via" label, system-generated note. Declaration and the seal box are on only in Tally style. |

A few options do more than show or hide:

- **Tax % column** off means no GST is charged at all, and the tax rows disappear from the totals. Bill of Supply and Delivery Challan turn it off for you.
- **Round-off line** rounds the grand total to the nearest rupee, and shows the difference. The default for new invoices is set in [Print & PDF](/docs/print-settings.html#round-off).
- **Business state** also hides the client's state, and **Tax ID** also hides the client's GSTIN.
- **Bank details** also hides your PAN, which prints in the bank block.
- **GST Cess % column** adds a Cess box to each row of the form. The printed invoice shows cess as one line in the totals.
- Hiding HSN, Discount, Place of Supply, state or Tax ID also hides the matching box in the form.

When **Declaration** is on, a box appears to change its wording. It starts as the standard "We declare that this invoice shows the actual price of the goods described and that all particulars are true and correct."

Hide all turns off everything in the header, client, invoice, items, totals and footer groups at once. Reset to default puts every option back as it was on a fresh install, including currency, paper size, recurring, TDS, TCS and reverse charge.

## The "system-generated invoice" note

In the Footer group, **Note: system-generated invoice** adds this line below the terms:

**Note:** This is a system-generated invoice. No signature or stamp is required.

It is off unless you turn it on. If you use it, consider turning the signature block off too, so the invoice does not contradict itself.

## Paper size

| Option | Size |

| A4 Portrait (default) | 210 × 297 mm |

| A4 Landscape | 297 × 210 mm |

| A5 Portrait (compact) | 148 × 210 mm |

| A5 Landscape (2 per A4 sheet) | 210 × 148 mm |

| US Letter | 216 × 279 mm |

| US Legal | 216 × 356 mm |

| B5 | 176 × 250 mm |

| 80mm Thermal (POS receipt) | 72 mm printable |

| 76mm Thermal (kitchen printer) | 68 mm printable |

| 58mm Thermal (compact / mobile) | 48 mm printable |

| 112mm Thermal (wide receipt) | 104 mm printable |

| Custom size | Width 30 to 500 mm, height 50 to 1200 mm |

For a custom size, enter the printer's printable width, not the roll width. Anything under 100 mm wide prints as a receipt. The quick buttons 40mm, 76mm, 90mm and 110mm fill in common rolls.

A client can have their own preferred paper size, which is used when you pick them on a new invoice.

## Thermal printer settings

When a thermal size is chosen, three more settings appear:

| Font size | Small, Medium (the default) or Large |

| Compact mode | Tighter item rows. Off to start. |

| Cut mark at bottom | Prints a CUT HERE line, for printers without an automatic cutter. On to start. |

More receipt settings are in [Print Settings](/docs/print-settings.html#thermal). See also [Thermal receipt printing](/docs/thermal-printing.html).

## What prints: the header

- **Your side**: logo, business name, address with city and PIN, state, GSTIN, email and phone. Each can be hidden.
- **The invoice's side**: the title; for a proforma, "This is not a tax invoice"; for a credit note, "Against Invoice" and the original number; then the number, date and due date; and, for tax invoices and credit notes in India, **Reverse Charge** Yes or No.

With a letterhead set in Print Settings, the header is replaced by your letterhead.

## What prints: Bill To, Ship To and Place of Supply

- **BILL TO**: the client's name, address, state, GSTIN, email and phone.
- **SHIP TO**: only when a different delivery address is entered.
- **PLACE OF SUPPLY**: the state, with **Interstate (IGST)** or **Intrastate (CGST + SGST)** beside it.

## What prints: the items table

Columns, left to right: **#**, **Description** (with its longer note underneath), **HSN/SAC**, **Qty** with the unit, **Rate**, **Disc.** (only when a line has a discount), the tax columns, and **Amount**.

- Within your state: **CGST** and **SGST**, each with its rate and amount.
- Another state: one **IGST** column.
- Outside India: one column with the local tax name, such as VAT.

**Amount** is the line's value after discount and before tax. The tax is in the columns beside it.

## What prints: the totals

On the left, the **amount in words** and a **Scan to pay (UPI)** QR code with your UPI ID and the amount. The QR only prints on rupee invoices, with a UPI ID set and a total above zero.

On the right, in order: Subtotal, Discount, CGST and SGST or IGST, GST Cess, TCS, Discount on total, Round-off, and **Total Due**. For a credit note, the last line reads **Credit Amount**. With TDS, **Less: TDS** and **Net Receivable** follow.

## What prints: notices and footer

- **Reverse charge notice**, when turned on.
- **Composition declaration**, always on composition bills: "Composition taxable person, not eligible to collect tax on supplies."
- **BANK DETAILS**: "Pay via" label if on, account name, bank, account number and type, IFSC, SWIFT, and your PAN.
- **EXCHANGE RATE**, on foreign-currency invoices.
- **TERMS & CONDITIONS** and **NOTES**, compact or formatted.
- **Signature block**: your signature and stamp side by side, "Authorized Signatory", and your business name. It only prints when a signature or stamp has been uploaded.

Export and SEZ invoices print no LUT declaration by themselves. Use the **Export / International (LUT)** terms preset, or write your own.

## Watermarks

- **CANCELLED**, in red, on a cancelled invoice.
- **ESTIMATE**, very faint, on a proforma.
- Your own watermark, copy labels such as ORIGINAL and DUPLICATE, REPRINT, page numbers and QR codes come from [Print Settings](/docs/print-settings.html), and only on sheet paper, not receipts.

---

# Thermal receipt printing

URL: /docs/thermal-printing.html

Printing bills on a 58 mm or 80 mm receipt printer at a shop counter, from setting it up to what the receipt shows.

## Setting it up

- **Install the printer in Windows**Use the driver that came with it, set the paper size in the driver to your roll width, and make it your default printer, or pick it in the print window each time.
- **Choose the receipt size**On an invoice, open Customize and set **Paper / print size** to **80mm Thermal** or **58mm Thermal**. The app remembers it for your next invoice.
- **Try a test print**In [Print Settings](/docs/print-settings.html#how-it-saves), pick the **Thermal (80mm)** preview tab and click Test Print.
- **Print a real bill**Save the invoice, then click Print. A preview of the receipt opens; click Print again.

Picking the **Retail Shop** or **Restaurant** business type in [Print Settings](/docs/print-settings.html#business-type) sets sensible receipt defaults in one go.

## The print preview

On a receipt size, Print shows the receipt at 160% so you can read it. Its buttons:

| Print | Sends it to the printer. Shows "Sending…" while it works. |

| Download PDF | Saves and downloads a PDF instead, the same as Save & Download. |

| Cancel | Closes it. So does Esc . |

## Printing straight after saving

At a busy counter, turn on [Auto-print on save](/docs/print-settings.html#auto-print): Save & Download then prints the receipt as well, with no extra click. It can also be turned on for just one client, in their details.

## What a receipt shows

- Your logo (if turned on in Print Settings), business name in capitals, tagline, address, GSTIN and phone.
- The document type, such as TAX INVOICE, then the invoice number, reverse charge, date, and the client's name, GSTIN and phone.
- Each item: its name, then quantity × rate, GST rate and HSN, with the amount on the right. The amount is quantity × rate, before discount and tax.
- Subtotal, discount, CGST, SGST or IGST, cess, round-off and **TOTAL**.
- Amount in words, bank details, a UPI QR code with "Scan to pay via UPI", and notes.
- Your footer message, such as "Thank you for your business!", your email, the cut line and blank lines to tear against.

## What a receipt leaves out

To fit a narrow roll, receipts do not print: terms and conditions, the signature and stamp, extra pages, the due date, place of supply, client address, TCS, TDS, whole-bill discount lines, the exchange rate, watermarks, the reverse charge and composition notices, or the PDF style and colour. The custom invoice title is not used either.

If you need any of these, print that invoice on A4 or A5 instead.

## Changing how receipts look

Font, boldness, capitals, spacing, darkness, what is shown, the QR size, the footer message, the cut mark and feed lines are all in [Print Settings, Thermal receipts](/docs/print-settings.html#thermal).

## When a receipt prints badly

| Problem | Try |

| Text is cut off on the right | Use a smaller printable width: most 80 mm printers print 72 mm, and most 58 mm printers print 48 mm. Use **Custom size** if yours differs. |

| Print is faint | Set **Font weight** to Bold or Ultra bold, and **Thermal ink darkness** to Dark. |

| The printer jams or stops half-way | Turn on [Buffer-safe mode](/docs/print-settings.html#thermal-compatibility). |

| Blurry text, or nothing prints | Set **Thermal print method** to **Via PDF**. |

| Paper does not feed far enough to tear | Increase **Feed lines after cut**. |

---

# Dashboard

URL: /docs/dashboard.html

Your invoices at a glance: what you have sold, what you are owed, what is overdue, and every action you can take on an invoice.

## At the top

The count beside the title is every document for the business selected in the sidebar, including estimates, challans and cancelled invoices. New Invoice starts a blank invoice, and CSV import / export brings in or saves many invoices at once (see below). When a [PIN](/docs/settings.html#lock) is set, Lock locks the app straight away.

## The Getting started list

New installs show four steps. Each ticks itself off once you have really done it, and has a button that takes you there:

| Step | Done when | Button |

| Add your business details | A business name is saved | Open Settings |

| Make your first invoice | Any invoice exists | Start |

| Add your products or services | At least one product is saved | Open |

| Add bank details or UPI | A bank account or UPI ID is saved | Open Settings |

It disappears when all four are done, or when you close it with ✕. **Read the 5-minute guide** opens this documentation in your browser.

## The support card

Once you have made 10 invoices, a small card at the top asks, once a day, whether you would like to support the app, with how much users have given so far. Support with UPI opens [Support & About](/docs/shortcuts.html#support). Not today hides it until tomorrow and Hide for 30 days for a month. It never blocks your work and is never printed on an invoice.

## Overdue invoices and reminders

When any invoice is overdue, a red banner shows how many and how much is outstanding. Click the banner to show only overdue invoices.

Remind All lists each overdue invoice with the client, amount and phone number. Remind opens WhatsApp with a polite reminder already written, such as "Invoice INV/0012 for ₹11,800 was due on 5 Sep 2026. Kindly arrange the payment…".

## The four totals

| **Total Invoiced** | The total of your sales, including GST |

| **Tax Collected** | The GST on those sales |

| **Outstanding** | What clients still owe on unpaid and part-paid invoices |

| **Invoices** | How many sales documents there are |

They cover only the selected business and only real sales. Tax invoices, bills of supply and composition bills count. Credit notes are subtracted. Proforma estimates, delivery challans and cancelled invoices are left out. Foreign-currency sales are shown on their own line, never added to rupees.

## Low stock

If alerts are on in [Settings](/docs/settings.html#stock), products at or below your threshold scroll past under **Low stock**, like a news ticker, with **Out of Stock** in red or the number left in amber. Point at it to stop it; click one to open Products.

## Finding an invoice

| Search | By client name or invoice number |

| Financial year | All years, or one of the last five |

| Type | Any of the six document types |

| Status | Unpaid, Partial, Paid, Overdue or Cancelled |

| From / To | A range of invoice dates |

✕ clears all filters at once.

## Choosing the columns

Columns lets you show or hide: Date, Invoice #, Type, Client, Amount, Currency, Status, Due date, Print count and Actions. Currency, due date and print count are hidden to start. The **Paid** column is always shown. Your choice is remembered.

A yellow note icon next to a client means the invoice has a private note. Point at it to read it.

## Status

Each invoice is **Unpaid**, **Partial**, **Paid**, **Overdue** or **Cancelled**. Recording payments sets it for you. Each time the Dashboard opens, unpaid and part-paid invoices past their due date become Overdue, and the row shows how many days late they are.

You can also change it from the dropdown on the row. Choosing **Paid** records a payment for the rest of the balance, so your payment history stays complete.

Choosing **Unpaid** on a paid invoice takes back the payment that marking it Paid recorded, so the Paid column clears and Send reminder comes back. Payments you recorded yourself stay; delete them under Payment History if they were wrong.

Only sales get paid, so only Tax Invoices, Bills of Supply and Composition bills have this dropdown. Quotations, proformas and delivery challans show **Open**, or **Converted** once turned into an invoice; credit notes show **Issued**. A cancelled one shows **Cancelled**; Undo cancel is with its actions.

## Recording a payment

- **Open it**Click the ₹ Payment button on the invoice. The top line shows the total, what is paid, and the balance.
- **Fill it in**Enter **Amount Received**, the **Payment Date** (today to start), the **Payment Mode** (Bank Transfer, UPI, Cash, Cheque, Card or Other), and a note such as the transaction ID.
- **Record it**Click Record Payment. The status becomes Partial or Paid, and a printable receipt opens.

A cancelled invoice cannot take a payment; change its status back first.

If the amount is more than the balance, you are asked whether to record it as an overpayment. The extra is kept as the client's credit, to use on [their next invoice](/docs/invoices.html#client-credit).

Under **Payment History**, each payment has Receipt to reprint it, a pencil to edit it, and a bin to delete it. The status is worked out again after any change.

## The payment receipt

It shows your business details, **PAYMENT RECEIPT**, the receipt number, date, invoice, payment mode and note, "Received with thanks from" the client, the amount (in words for rupees), the invoice total, total paid and balance, and signature lines. Print Receipt prints it on A5.

## What you can do with an invoice

The row shows the actions you use most. The rest are in the ⋯ menu at the end of the row; it closes with Esc or a click elsewhere.

| 👁 View | Shows the invoice exactly as it prints, without opening the editor. Print prints it, Esc closes it. The slider at the bottom zooms the preview from 30% to 250% ( − and + step 10%); click the percentage to go back to the normal size. Zoom only changes the preview; the print is always full size. |

| Edit | Opens it on the invoice screen. |

| Duplicate | A new invoice with the same client and items, a new number and today's date. It starts Unpaid, with no payments. |

| Print | Prints the invoice straight away, without opening it, then returns to the Dashboard. |

| Convert to Tax Invoice | Quotations, proformas and delivery challans only, until they have been converted. See [Turning a quote into an invoice](/docs/invoices.html#proforma-to-invoice). |

| ₹ Payment | Record a payment, as above. |

| WhatsApp | On a phone, attaches the PDF through your phone's share menu. On a computer, WhatsApp does not let websites attach files, so the chat with the client opens (using the phone number saved for them) with the invoice details, and the PDF is downloaded for you to drag into the chat. |

| Send reminder | Shown for unpaid, part-paid and overdue invoices. Opens WhatsApp with a reminder suited to the situation. |

| Email | Opens your email program with the subject and a short message. Add the address and attach the PDF yourself. |

| Cancel | See Cancelling an invoice . |

A cancelled invoice keeps only View, Duplicate and Undo cancel. A quotation, proforma or challan already converted keeps only View and Duplicate, so it cannot be changed or converted twice. Opened, either one is read-only: you can download or print it, not change it. Payments they already have stay viewable from the ₹ button.

## Cancelling an invoice

Cancel asks first, then marks the invoice cancelled. It keeps its number, which GST requires, but no longer counts in totals, reports or GST returns, and any stock it used goes back. If you saved or printed its PDF, the copy in the Saved Invoices folder gets **CANCELLED** across every page.

To undo it, click the Undo cancel arrow among the row's actions and answer **Yes, undo**. It goes back to Unpaid, Partial or Paid, from its payments, the stock is taken out again, and its saved PDF is put back exactly as it was. A cancelled invoice is never shown as overdue.

## Importing and exporting invoices as CSV

For moving invoices in from Excel, Tally or another program, or out to your CA.

- **Open it**Click CSV import / export at the top of the Dashboard.
- **Start from the template**Template downloads a CSV with the right columns and an example. Fill it in with Excel or Google Sheets and save it as CSV. Export all as CSV gives what you already have, in the same columns.
- **Choose the file**Choose CSV file shows what will happen **before** anything is saved: how many are ready, which already exist and are skipped, and every row with a problem (a bad date, a missing rate). Rows with problems are not imported; fix the file and choose it again.
- **Import**Click Import. A message says how many were imported and skipped.

One row per item. Rows with the same invoice number make one invoice; give the client, date and other invoice details on the first row (later rows may leave them blank). Column names are matched loosely, so **Qty** or **Quantity**, **GSTIN** or **Client GSTIN** both work. Dates can be 2026-10-01, 01-10-2026 or 01/10/2026 (day first).

| Column | What to put |

| Invoice Number, Invoice Date | Required. |

| Invoice Type | Tax Invoice (if blank), Bill of Supply, Composition, Quotation, Proforma, Delivery Challan or Credit Note. |

| Due Date | Optional. |

| Client Name, Client GSTIN, Client State, Client Address, Client Country | The name is required. A client already in Clients fills in the rest. The state can be a name, a 2-digit code, or left to the GSTIN. |

| Place of Supply | Only if it differs from the client's state. |

| Item Name, HSN/SAC, Quantity, Unit, Rate | Rate is required. A product of the same name fills in a missing HSN or unit. |

| Discount | Rupees off that line. |

| GST %, Cess % | Such as 18 and 0. |

| Prices Include Tax | Yes if the rates already include GST. |

| Notes | Printed on the invoice. |

| Bill Discount, Round Off | For the whole invoice: rupees off after tax, and Yes to round the total to the rupee. |

GST, CGST + SGST or IGST and the totals are worked out exactly as on the invoice screen. An invoice number that already exists is **skipped, never overwritten**. Two different invoices with the same number (for example, numbering that restarts each year) are refused: give one of them its own number.

Two choices before importing: **Add new clients to Clients**, and **Take sold quantities out of product stock**. Leave stock off when importing old invoices whose stock you have already counted.

## Printing many invoices as one PDF

The **Quick print** buttons combine invoices from the list as it is currently filtered into one PDF, one invoice per page:

- All shown: every invoice in the list
- Unpaid: only those marked Unpaid, not part-paid or overdue
- Overdue and Paid

For more than five invoices, a message shows how far it has got. For more than 100, you are asked first.

## Ticking several invoices

Tick the box on each row, or the box in the header for every visible row. A bar appears with:

| Mark paid , Mark unpaid , Mark overdue | Change them all, after asking. Mark paid records a payment for each balance. |

| Export JSON | Saves the ticked invoices to a file, which can be imported as a backup. |

| Bulk PDF | Combines the ticked invoices into one PDF, useful for your CA or for filing. Cancel stops it part-way and keeps what is done. |

| Cancel invoices | Cancels the ticked invoices, after asking, and puts their stock back. Marking cancelled invoices as anything else brings them back and takes the stock out again. |

Ticks stay when you change the filters, so check the count before acting.

---

# Clients

URL: /docs/clients.html

Everyone you bill, what each one owes, their account statement, and how quickly they pay.

## The client list

Every client you have saved, and every name you have invoiced, appears as a card, with the ones who owe the most at the top. **Search clients…** finds them by name.

Each card shows the number of invoices, the state and GSTIN, and three figures: **Total**, **Paid**, and **Outstanding** in red, or **Overpaid** in blue if they have paid too much. Only real sales count: credit notes are subtracted, and quotations, estimates, challans and cancelled invoices are left out. Click a card to open it.

Your client list is shared by all your businesses, since the same customer may buy from each.

## Adding and editing a client

Add Client opens the form. The same form opens from the invoice screen.

| Field | What to know |

| Client / Business Name | Required |

| Address, City, PIN Code | The postal label changes with the country |

| Country | Starts as your own country. Changing it clears the state. |

| State | A list for India, a text box for countries without one |

| GSTIN | Checked when you leave the box, as on the invoice: the state is filled in if blank, and typos and a mismatched state are pointed out. See [What the GSTIN check tells you](/docs/invoices.html#gstin-check). |

| Email, Phone | The phone number is used for WhatsApp |

| SEZ unit / Developer | India only. Charges IGST whatever their state, under section 16 of the IGST Act. |

Under **Print preferences (optional)**, a client can have a **preferred paper size**, a **preferred currency** and **Auto-print on save**. They are applied whenever you pick this client on a new invoice.

## A client's account

Open a card to see all their invoices, newest first, with date, number, type, amount and status. Each row has buttons to edit, duplicate, share on WhatsApp, email or delete it. The status can be changed from the row too; choosing Paid records a payment for the balance, as on the Dashboard.

At the bottom: Edit Client and Delete Client, or, for a name that was never saved, Save as Client. Deleting a client only removes them from your saved list; their invoices stay.

Deleting an invoice here moves it to the Trash for 30 days. It can be restored from [Settings, Trash bin](/docs/backup.html#trash). For an invoice already given to a client, [cancel it](/docs/dashboard.html#cancel) instead, so its number stays in your records.

## Ageing: who is slow to pay

When a client owes money, a strip shows it split by how late it is: **Current** (up to 30 days), **31-60 days**, **61-90 days** and **90+ days**. Lateness is counted from the due date, or from the invoice date when there is none.

## Statement and ageing PDFs

- **Statement PDF**: their whole account, from your business to theirs. It has a summary of invoices, total billed, paid and outstanding, then every invoice, credit note and payment with a running balance marked Dr (they owe you) or Cr (you owe them), and a closing balance. Send it when a bill is disputed.
- **Aging PDF**: only what is outstanding, invoice by invoice, with how many days old each is, and totals for each group. Amounts over 60 days are in red. Useful for collection calls.

## Importing clients from a spreadsheet

Import CSV adds clients from a CSV file, one per row. Save your spreadsheet as CSV first. The first row must name the columns:

| Column heading | Holds |

| name (or client , client name ) | Required. Rows without a name are skipped. |

| address , state , gstin , email , phone | Optional |

```
name,address,state,gstin,email,phone
Sharma Traders,12 MG Road,Punjab,03AAAAA0000A1Z5,accounts@sharma.example,9876543210
```

Clients you already have (same name) are skipped, so importing the same file twice is safe. Other columns, such as city or PIN, are ignored.

---

# Products and stock

URL: /docs/products.html

Save what you sell once, then pick it on every invoice. Stock goes down as you sell and up as you buy.

## The product list

Products in the sidebar opens your catalogue. The table shows name, HSN/SAC, rate, GST %, unit and stock. Point at a name to see its description. Search by name or HSN.

## Adding a product or service

| Field | What to know |

| Product / Service Name | Required |

| HSN / SAC Code | HSN for goods, SAC for services |

| Purchase Price | What you pay the supplier. Filled in on new purchase bills. |

| Selling Price | What you charge. Filled in on new invoices, and shown as the rate in the list. |

| GST % | Type the rate, such as 18 |

| Unit | Pcs to start, or any unit from the list, including your own [custom units](/docs/invoices.html#items) |

| Stock Quantity | How many you have now |

| Description | For your own reference |

Deleting a product does not change invoices that used it.

## Changing many products at once

Bulk edit turns the list into a grid you can type in: name, HSN/SAC, purchase price, selling price, GST %, unit and stock. Changed rows are highlighted. Save changes saves them all in one go; Cancel drops them. Search first to edit only some products.

A product needs a name, and GST % must be 0 to 100; if a row breaks a rule, nothing is saved and you are told which product to fix.

Print / PDF, Excel and CSV above the list save the products shown, with prices, GST and stock.

## How stock is counted

- **Selling**: saving a Tax Invoice, Bill of Supply, Composition bill or Delivery Challan takes the quantity out, for rows picked from your products. Change the quantity later and save, and only the difference moves.
- **Returns**: a Credit Note puts the quantity back.
- **Quotations and proformas** move no stock. The invoice you convert them into does.
- **Buying**: saving a [purchase bill](/docs/purchases.html#stock) adds the quantity in, and adds any new item to your products.
- **Cancelling** an invoice puts its stock back; un-cancelling takes it out again.

**Out of Stock** shows in red at zero or below. Purchases and deletions never take stock below zero; selling more than you have does, so you notice.

## Low-stock alerts

A product at or below your threshold shows its stock in amber here, is listed on the Dashboard, and adds to the notification bell. The threshold is 5 to start; change it, or turn alerts off, in [Settings](/docs/settings.html#stock). It is one threshold for every product.

## Importing products from a spreadsheet

Import CSV loads a price list. The first row must name the columns:

| Column heading | Holds |

| name (or product , product name ) | Required |

| hsn (or hsn code , sac ) | HSN or SAC code |

| rate (or price ) | Selling price |

| gst% (or tax% , taxpercent , tax ) | GST rate, such as 18. Note: no space before the %. |

| unit | Nos if left out |

| stock (or quantity ) | Opening stock |

| description | Optional |

```
name,hsn,rate,gst%,unit,stock
A4 Paper Ream,4802,280,12,Nos,50
Website Maintenance,998314,5000,18,Month,0
```

Products you already have (same name) are skipped, so importing the same file twice is safe.

---

# Payment receipts

URL: /docs/receipts.html

Receipts for money you have received, whether against an invoice or not, ready to print.

## The receipts list

Receipts lists every receipt, newest first: date, receipt number, client, the invoice it was against, amount and mode. Search by client or receipt number. Each row can be printed, edited or deleted.

Recording a payment on the [Dashboard](/docs/dashboard.html#payments) makes its own receipt, which you print from the payment history there.

## Making a receipt

- **Start it**Click New Receipt.
- **Pick the invoice, if there is one****Quick Select, Unpaid Invoices** lists up to 50 unpaid sales invoices. Picking one fills in the client, the amount still owed and the invoice number.
- **Fill in the rest**Date, **Received From** (required), **Amount** (required), **Payment Mode**, **Reference / Transaction No**, **Against Invoice** and a note.
- **Save**Save Receipt gives it the next receipt number.

When **Against Invoice** exactly matches one of your invoice numbers, the payment is also recorded on that invoice, and its status becomes Partial or Paid. If it does not match any invoice, the receipt is saved on its own and you are told so.

## Receipt numbers

Receipts have their own series, starting RCP, and follow your [invoice number format](/docs/settings.html#invoice-numbers): separator, financial year and digits. If you set a brand prefix, it is used for receipts too. The next number is given when you save, unless you typed your own, which is kept.

## Printing

The print button opens the receipt in a new window and your print dialog. It shows your business name, address and GSTIN, **PAYMENT RECEIPT**, the receipt number, date, who paid, how, the reference and invoice, the amount in figures and words, any note, and lines for **Received By** and **Authorized Signatory**. If nothing happens, allow pop-ups for the app in your browser.

## Deleting a receipt

Deleting a receipt removes only the receipt. A payment it recorded on an invoice stays there; delete that from the invoice's payment history on the Dashboard if it was a mistake.

---

# Recurring invoices

URL: /docs/recurring.html

Invoices that repeat on a schedule, such as a monthly retainer, rent or an annual maintenance contract.

## Two ways to set one up

- **From an invoice** (recommended): make the first invoice as usual, and under Customize tick [Make this a recurring invoice](/docs/invoice-options.html#recurring). This keeps everything on the invoice, including taxes, terms and options, and lets you set **Every N** and an end date or number of invoices.
- **From the Recurring screen**: New Template with a client, frequency, next date, when to stop, type and simple item lines.

## The New Template form

| Quick Select Client | Fills in the client's name, GSTIN, state and address |

| Client Name | Required |

| Client GSTIN | Optional |

| Frequency | Weekly, Monthly, Quarterly or Yearly |

| Every | 1 to 12. Monthly with 3 means every three months. |

| Next Due Date | The 1st of next month, to start |

| Stop | **Never (until I stop it)**, **On a specific date**, or **After N invoices** |

| Invoice Type | Any of the six types |

| Line Items | Description, Qty, Rate and GST%. At least one item with a rate is needed. |

## The template list

Each template shows the client, how often (such as "Every 3 months"), type, amount, next due date and whether it is **Active** or **Paused**. Its buttons: ▶ Generate Now, Pause or Activate, Edit, and Delete. Editing keeps everything the form does not show, such as terms and options from the original invoice. Deleting a template stops future invoices; invoices already made stay.

When templates are due, a banner lists them, with a button for each to create its invoice now.

## How invoices are created automatically

A few seconds after the app starts, and then once a day while it is running, every active template whose date has come creates its invoice, with a fresh number and that day's date. Its next date then moves on by the schedule, and it stops at its end condition.

The notification bell tells you how many were created. They appear on the Dashboard, ready to check and send.

If the app was closed for a while, one invoice is created each time it catches up, so a missed month is not skipped.

## Generate Now

▶ creates the invoice straight away, even if the template is paused or not yet due, exactly as the automatic run would: same tax, a fresh number, today's date. Its next date moves on by the schedule and it counts towards "After N invoices". Once a template has reached its end, it says so instead. Open the new invoice from the Dashboard to check it before sending.

---

# Purchase bills

URL: /docs/purchases.html

Record every supplier bill, so the GST you paid comes back as input tax credit and your stock stays right. Includes reading a bill from a photo.

## The purchase list

At the top, **Total Purchases**, **GST (ITC Eligible)** and **Entries** add up what is shown. Search by supplier, invoice number or GSTIN, and pick a financial year (one of the last five) or All years.

The table shows date, supplier, GSTIN, invoice number, taxable value, tax, total, status and actions, with totals at the bottom. Each row has:

- the eye, to view the bill without downloading anything;
- the pencil, to edit it;
- the bin, to delete it.

The view has Download PDF.

## Adding a purchase bill

Add Purchase opens the form:

| Field | What to know |

| Date | Today to start |

| Payment Status | Unpaid, Paid or Partial |

| Supplier Name | Required. Suppliers you have used before are suggested; picking one fills in their GSTIN, address and whether they are in another state. |

| Supplier GSTIN | 15 characters |

| Supplier Address | Optional. Printed on the purchase bill PDF. |

| Invoice Number | Required. The supplier's invoice number. |

| Note | Optional |

| Inter-state purchase | See Suppliers in another state |

Each item row has **Name**, **HSN**, **Qty**, **Rate**, **Tax %** (0, 0.1, 0.25, 3, 5, 12, 18 or 28, or Other… for any rate) and **Cess %**. Typing a name suggests your products and items from earlier bills, and fills in the HSN, rate and tax you used before. Clicking Qty, Rate or Cess selects what is in it, so typing replaces it.

A bill needs a supplier name, an invoice number, and at least one item with a quantity and rate.

## Round-off

If the supplier rounded their total to the rupee, tick **Apply round-off** so yours matches, for example ₹1,234.56 becomes ₹1,235. It is off to start, since most bills already match the line items.

## Suppliers in another state

If the supplier charged IGST because they are in a different state, the bill is **Inter-state purchase**, and the credit goes to IGST in GSTR-3B rather than CGST and SGST. The box ticks itself when you type the supplier's full GSTIN: its first two digits are their state code, compared with your business's. You can still change it for the rare exception.

## Paying suppliers

Change a bill's status straight from the coloured **Status** dropdown in the list: **Unpaid** in amber, **Paid** in green, **Partial** in purple.

## What saving does to your products

Each item on the bill is matched to your products by name:

- **A product you already have**: its stock goes up by the quantity, and its purchase price is updated. When you edit a bill, only the difference is added, and a row you remove is taken back out.
- **A new item**: it is added to your products, with the rate as both purchase and selling price, and the quantity as its stock. Check its selling price afterwards.
- **Deleting a bill** takes its quantities back out of stock.

## Reading a bill from a photo

- **Open it**Click Import from image (OCR).
- **Choose the picture**Click or drag a photo or scan of the bill: PNG, JPG or WebP, up to 8 MB. PDFs are not accepted; take a screenshot of the page instead.
- **Read it**Click Extract fields. It takes a few seconds, with a percentage showing progress.
- **Check everything**The supplier, GSTIN, invoice number, date and grand total are filled in, with the line items it could read: name, HSN, quantity, rate and GST rate. Items that match your saved products take your stored HSN and GST rate. Fix anything wrong, add or remove rows.
- **Use it**Use these values opens the purchase form with it all filled in. Check it once more and save.

Everything is read on your computer, in English, with no internet needed and nothing uploaded. Sharp, straight, well-lit photos read best. If no items are found but a total is, one line with the total is added, for you to split into the real items.

The purchase form does not take the tax breakdown or grand total from the photo: it works them out from the items, so check they match the bill. Tick **Inter-state purchase** yourself if the bill shows IGST.

## For your accountant

Print / PDF, Excel and CSV above the list give the purchase register for the current search and year, oldest first, with a total row: date, supplier, GSTIN, invoice number, taxable amount, tax, cess, inter-state, round-off, total, status and note.

## Importing purchase bills from CSV

- **Open it**Click CSV import / export at the top of Purchases.
- **Start from the template**Template downloads a CSV with the right columns and an example. Fill it in with Excel or Google Sheets and save it as CSV. Export all as CSV gives what you already have, in the same columns.
- **Choose the file**Choose CSV file shows what will happen **before** anything is saved: how many are ready, which already exist and are skipped, and every row with a problem (a bad date, a missing rate). Rows with problems are not imported; fix the file and choose it again.
- **Import**Click Import. A message says how many were imported and skipped.

One row per item. Rows with the same supplier and invoice number make one bill. Columns: Invoice Number, Invoice Date, Supplier Name, Supplier GSTIN, Supplier Address, Item Name, HSN/SAC, Quantity, Rate, GST %, Cess %, Inter-state, Payment Status (Unpaid, Partial or Paid) and Note.

A bill already entered (same supplier and number, matched by GSTIN or by name) is skipped. If **Inter-state** is blank, it is worked out from the supplier's GSTIN. Quantities are added to product stock, as when you type a bill in.

## "Not assigned to a business"

If you have more than one business, bills saved before you started keeping them separate show under all of them, with a banner. Assign to moves them all to the business now selected. Only do this if they belong to it. The same banner appears on Expenses, Recurring and Receipts.

---

# Expenses

URL: /docs/expenses.html

Costs that are not stock, such as rent, electricity, software or travel, for your profit and loss and for the GST credit on them.

## The expense list

**Total Expenses**, **GST Paid (ITC)** and **Entries** add up what is shown. Search by description, vendor or bill number, and filter by category and financial year. The table shows date, description, category, vendor, amount, GST and payment mode, with totals at the bottom.

## Adding an expense

| Field | What to know |

| Date | Today to start |

| Category | See the list below. Other to start. |

| Description | Required, such as "AWS Hosting - March" |

| Amount (incl. GST) | Required. The full amount you paid. |

| GST % (for ITC) | The GST rate on the bill. The GST inside the amount is worked out and shown underneath. |

| Vendor Name, Vendor GSTIN | Needed to claim the credit |

| Invoice / Bill No | Optional |

| Payment Mode | Bank Transfer, UPI, Cash, Cheque, Card or Other |

| Inter-state expense | Tick when the vendor charged IGST, as with cloud and software firms billing from another state |

| Note | Optional |

## Categories

Office Rent, Utilities, Internet & Phone, Software & Tools, Travel, Meals & Entertainment, Office Supplies, Salary & Wages, Professional Fees, Insurance, Marketing & Ads, Raw Materials, Shipping & Courier, Repairs & Maintenance, Bank Charges, GST Paid, Asset Purchase, Personal / Drawings, and Other.

The [Income Tax](/docs/income-tax.html) screen leaves out **Personal / Drawings** and **Asset Purchase** when working out business income, since they are not business expenses for tax. The [profit and loss report](/docs/reports.html) includes every category.

## How the GST credit is used

The GST on each expense is added to your input tax credit in [GSTR-3B](/docs/gst-returns.html#gstr-3b): to IGST if the expense is inter-state, otherwise split between CGST and SGST. Only claim credit you are entitled to: food, personal spending and bills without the vendor's GSTIN usually do not qualify. Check against GSTR-2B.

## For your accountant

The expense statement: Print / PDF, Excel and CSV above the list save the rows shown, oldest first, with a total: date, description, category, amount, GST amount, GST %, vendor, vendor GSTIN, invoice number, payment mode, inter-state and note. Choose the year and a category, or search, first: for example, all Rent for the year.

---

# GST returns

URL: /docs/gst-returns.html

GSTR-1 and GSTR-3B built from the invoices, purchases and expenses you have already entered, checked against GSTR-2B, and ready to upload to the GST portal.

**The app prepares, you file**
The app works out the figures and makes the files. It does not log in to the GST portal. Filing is always done by you, or your CA, on gst.gov.in.

## Choosing the period

At the top, pick **Monthly**, **Quarterly (QRMP)** or **Full Year**:

- **Monthly**: a month and year. This month to start.
- **Quarterly**: Q1 (Apr-Jun), Q2 (Jul-Sep), Q3 (Oct-Dec) or Q4 (Jan-Mar), and a year. The year is the calendar year of those months, so the Jan-Mar 2027 quarter is Q4 with 2027.
- **Full Year**: a financial year, such as FY 2026-27.

Everything on the screen follows the period and the business selected in the sidebar.

## What is included

- **GSTR-1 and GSTR-3B** use tax invoices and credit notes only.
- Proforma estimates, bills of supply, composition bills and delivery challans are left out. So are cancelled invoices.
- The **Documents issued** table lists every kind of document you numbered, as the portal asks.
